messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — Q1 month close: found a mismatch in the revenue schedule for the pricing experiment SKUs. Invoice INV-7892 shows prepay applied to promo units but the deferred revenue schedule didn’t pick up the allocation. Can finance take a look? Mentioning @Ajay Patel @Blake Rivera

Ajay Patel: On it. Do we have the invoice PDF and the GL posting ID? If you paste the posting I can trace the JE and see what hit deferred rev.

Maria Chen: Posting is JE-2026-4432 (acct 4100 Deferred Revenue). Invoice uploaded to Drive: https://redwood/drive/inv/INV-7892 — it looks like a mid-cycle promo was auto-applied.

Blake Rivera: FWIW Ops changed the ratecard mid-billing window for that customer, so proration may be the culprit. I’ll check the usage split and the billing run logs.

Eloise - RevRec: Quick Q — are we treating these experiment credits as contra-revenue or as a reduction of gross billed revenue for revrec? Policy says trial credits are typically contra-revenue unless the customer prepaid for a contractual bundle. Need clear treatment before we reverse deferrals.

Maria Chen: This was a PLG pricing experiment with auto-credited tokens (not a contractual prepay). Customer moved to paid on 3/28. We need guidance on cutoff and whether to recognize a partial portion in March.

Ajay Patel: Proposal: reclass 60% of the prepaid balance from deferred to revenue pro-rata for March close, and leave an accrual for the remaining 40% expected to be used over the 90-day experiment window. I’ll draft the JE. Approvals?

Eloise - RevRec: Approve in principle. Need a short memo with the calculation: cohort count, usage units, effective date, FX impact (customer billed in EUR). Also confirm if credits are refundable or purely promotional. If material (> $50k) we’ll need VP Finance sign-off.

Maria Chen: Credits are non-refundable promo tokens per the experiment terms (see experiment doc in Drive). I’ve uploaded the cohort CSV to #finance-docs and dropped the link in Drive.

Blake Rivera: Noted. Also saw that the AP invoice from our vendor didn’t include the rate override in line detail. I’ll loop Revenue Ops to confirm which rate was applied programmatically vs. the billing export.

rev-bot: Reminder — month-end close checklist: deferral & accrual JEs due by 23:00 PT on the close date :alarm_clock: Follow the template in /finance/templates/deferral-je.md

Ajay Patel: I’ll prepare the JE using the template and tag @Eloise for sign-off. Maria — can you drop the experiment cohort headcount and the total promo USD exposure by EOD so I can compute the reclass?

Maria Chen: Sent the CSV and a short calc sheet to Drive and linked in #finance-docs. The USD exposure (gross) is ~14,200 USD before FX.

Eloise - RevRec: Thanks. If the net impact after FX is under $50k we can handle at my level; otherwise I’ll escalate. Please include the FX rate and the derivation in the memo.

Blake Rivera: Ops confirmed — rate applied was a 50% promo override; adjusted pro-rata calc attached in Drive.

Maria Chen: Great. Ajay/Eloise — let us know if you need any other backup for approval routing. I’ll hold on booking anything until sign-off. :thumbsup:
